name: triggers
about: Trigger points: when the playlist's voice-overs fire (seconds after the start of the track, fake clock, 50 ms ticks; each fire is a Play on Top with no playlist entry). `fires` is what the Python player measured (it includes the tick); `ideal_fires` is the time at which the playhead reaches `at` ((at - A) after the start, plus whole passes in a loop); another engine compares its own times with the IDEAL ones within `tolerance_s`.

add the trigger points
play track 0 and start counting
tick every 50 ms for run_s (the seek, if any, at seek.at_s of play)

scenario.input: per row: trim {in: A} (none for A = 0), ONE trigger point at `at` (set_triggers rounds `at` to 1 ms), play track 0 from the start, tick every 50 ms for 0.4 s; `first_fire_t_s` = seconds after the start of play, null = never fired

point_at_or_near_A_start_at_A._info: a start at A (offset 0): a point at A or up to 50 ms later fires on the first tick (it is already reached when the first tick looks), a point 1 ms BEFORE A never fires (Before A: `at >= A - 1e-6` is required), a point later than the first tick fires when the playhead reaches it. Margin: the point must be at >= A (to the microsecond); there is no tolerance on the A - 1 ms side

scenario.input: per row: trim {in: 2.0}, ONE trigger point at `at`, _start(playlist 0, track 0, offset = offset_s) (a resume / seek-style start: offset in FILE seconds; start_s = where the sound begins), tick every 50 ms for 0.4 s

point_near_A_start_with_offset._info_tolerance_by_key: start_s is the exact float seconds max(A, offset) where the sound begins (not a frame count), offset_s and at are the inputs: positions in file seconds, compared within one sample; the times of the first fire use tolerance_s (one tick)
point_near_A_start_with_offset._info: `ideal_fired` is the contract: start_s == A: every point at >= A fires; otherwise a point behind the start (at < start_s) never fires, a point at least one tick (0.05 s) ahead fires when the playhead reaches it (`ideal_t_s` = at - start_s, within tolerance_s), and a point inside the first tick after the start is undefined (null, not compared). `fired` / `first_fire_t_s` are what Python did. Where `python_differs` is true Python deviates from the contract (quirk 13: part-way starts within 0.06 s of A are 'fresh' and fire the points between A and the start, although the playhead is already past them)

target_ready_after_1s._info: the point is at 5 s but vo.wav is decoded only at 6 s of play: the point is kept waiting (it is 'due') and fires on the first tick after the target is ready, 1 s late. The wait is not a fixed delay: the voice-over starts as soon as it can

target_never_ready._info: vo.wav is never decoded: the point waits and is then given up on (a notice 'could not be loaded'): nothing fires and the track is not disturbed. How long it waits (30 s in Python, TRIG_WAIT_S) is an implementation limit, not contract: a port may wait less or more, but must give up at some point and must not fire a voice-over that is minutes late

target_never_ready_does_not_block_next_p._info: the first point is still waiting for its target when the second one is reached: a point that waits does not hold up the points after it. The second fires at 10 s as if the first did not exist (and the first never fires)

scenario.config: top_track_pct per row (the other Play on Top / ducking settings are the defaults)
steps: set top_track_pct
two trigger points: vo2 (8 s) at 10 s, vo (3 s) at 12 s
play track 0
tick every 50 ms to 10.2 s and read the decks
tick on to 12.7 s and read them again
tick on to 20.2 s (vo2 ended at 18 s) and read them a third time

voice_level_and_second_point._info: the voice-over plays at top_track_pct / 100 (a plain volume, no fade-in; gain 1.0: level match never applies to a trigger voice-over); it becomes the live deck. The second point (12 s), reached while vo2 is still on top, is SKIPPED: nothing is queued, nothing overlaps (still exactly one top deck, vo2, nothing fires). At 20 s the voice-over is over, the live deck is the main track again and still nothing has fired a second time (a queued point would have started at 18 s). The same rule as a Play on Top by hand: a second Play on Top REPLACES the first, but a trigger point never does

steps: trigger point at 2 s on track 0
play track 0 (the real _duck_loop runs under the fake clock, 10 ms per step)
tick every 50 ms; at 4.0 s start track 1 with play(0, 1, crossfade_ms)
read the decks and the ducking state at the listed times

new_track_cut_while_voice_on_top._info: the voice-over fires at 2 s and ducks the background; at 4 s a new track is started with a CUT (Go with the Cut setting, /take, /cut, next, play: all `play(p, t)`). stop_all(): the voice-over, the background and the ducking state are all gone at once (gr 0, nothing armed) and the new track plays at full level, alone. No release ramp. `vol` is the deck volume at the tick (fade curves as in fades.json); `ducked` = the background multiplier is below 0.99; gr_db and duck_armed are Python's internal ducking state (_info_python_*, not compared). A deck that has just finished its fade is still listed at that tick and removed on the next one (not compared: no row at 5.0 s)

steps: trigger point at 2 s on track 0

new_track_crossfade_while_voice_on_top._info: same, but the new track is started with a 1000 ms CROSSFADE: EVERY running deck, the voice-over included, fades out (and is removed when its fade is done) while the new track fades in. The new track is not part of the ducked background: it comes in at its own level (duck 1.0) and is never ducked; the ducking loop keeps the dip on the old background until the voice-over is gone, then releases (500 ms) and ends. `vol` is the deck volume at the tick (fade curves as in fades.json); `ducked` = the background multiplier is below 0.99; gr_db and duck_armed are Python's internal ducking state (_info_python_*, not compared). A deck that has just finished its fade is still listed at that tick and removed on the next one (not compared: no row at 5.0 s)
